segments.text: Five food additives I avoid and they're healthy alternatives.
Everything I'm about to show you is all backed
by published medical data, not just one, but multiple sources.
Number one is fructose.
It's fine when you eat it with fruit
because of the fiber that's associated with it.
However, when you have commercially prepared
crystalline fructose or high fructose corn syrup,
the body absorbs it and it has damaging effects.
It drives dopamine receptors down and is highly addictive.
It does not satiate you the same way
that normal table sugar does,
keeps you hungry compared to regular sugar,
produces more body fat and physical inactivity.
In other words, it makes you more sedentary,
but also inhibits three enzymes critical
for mitochondrial function,
AMPA kinase, ACADL, and CPT1.
It's also been shown to contribute
to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
And yes, finally, it causes what's called leaky gut.
When fructose is absorbed without fiber,
it causes the tight junctions in the epithelial cells.
Those are the cells within your intestinal walls
to start to separate and there is some permeability
that happens where the stuff that's flowing
through those intestines permeates causing inflammation
and all other sorts of inflammatory syndromes.
Number two on the list is high fructose corn syrup.
We just talked about fructose, now you put it into a syrup
and it does all of the same things
that crystalline fructose does, but even more.
It contributes to cancer.
It can contribute to metabolic disorders
and dopamine down regulation even without obesity
being present.
It's been shown to contribute to diabetes
and it puts you at greater risk for heart disease.
For both of these, what are healthy alternatives?
Well, we could use monk fruit, stevia, or aulose.
Number three is synthetic food dyes.
These are red 40, yellow number five, and yellow number six.
A 2023 study showed that red 40 causes DNA damage
and colonic inflammation and affects the gut microbiome.
A 2022 study showed that synthetic food dyes
are linked to ADHD in children,
and a 2015 study showed that it is linked directly to cancer.
Healthy alternatives for synthetic dyes
and the ingredients you wanna look for things
such as paprika and turmeric for yellow,
for the reds, beet juice, blueberries, beta carotene,
cherries, beet powder, pomegranate juice,
cranberries, or strawberries.
Those are all natural red dyes.
Number four is nitrates found commonly
in deli-sliced meat, cross-sets meats,
bacon, those sorts of things.
A 2022 study showed that nitrates
show an increased risk of cancer when ingested.
Alternatives for nitrates when it comes to meat,
simply buying fresh meat rather than the pre-packaged stuff
or look for packaged meat, deli sliced meat
that says no nitrates.
Number five, agave syrup.
I know it's supposed to be healthy for us.
However, it is simply high fructose corn syrup
masquerading as this thing called agave syrup.
Because the fiber's been removed
and it's now just a syrup
and it's very high in fructose,
usually about 57 to 90% fructose,
you have the same effects as high fructose corn syrup
and that crystalline fructose happening
that I mentioned earlier.
Again, great alternatives for this sweetener
would be Stevia or Alulose.
Can we avoid all of these all the time?
Probably not.
Do I get some of these things in mind nutrition
from time to time?
Sure, absolutely, because life is about balance.
However, the more education you have,
the better choices you can make
for your own personal health goals.
And if you want this in a simple form,
I do have it in a downloadable PDF.
That link is in my profile, in my link tree.
It's totally free.
You don't have to fill out a form or anything.
Just click the link.
It'll take you right to the PDF.
If you want more help with your fitness and nutrition, I'm here for you and so is my team.
There's always details in my profile for my online one-on-one fitness and nutrition coaching
or you can just simply go to coachgabby.com.
Cheers to a happy, healthier, more energetic you.
